name: Rifaximin
route_note: Oral tablets two or three times daily; minimal systemic absorption
targets: rpoB (bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase β subunit)

discovery.note: A pyrido-imidazole derivative of rifamycin SV designed to be essentially non-absorbed from the gut. Year is the priority date of the Alfa Farmaceutici patent on imidazo-rifamycin derivatives (US 4,341,785; Marchi and Montecchi).

tagline: Non-absorbed antibiotic for hepatic encephalopathy, IBS-D and traveller's diarrhoea
summary: Rifaximin is a rifamycin antibiotic that stays almost entirely in the gut. It reduces recurrence of hepatic encephalopathy, treats irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhoea and treats traveller's diarrhoea caused by non-invasive E. coli.
mechanism: Rifaximin binds the β subunit of bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, blocking transcription. Because less than 0.4% is absorbed, high concentrations are achieved in the intestinal lumen.
In hepatic encephalopathy it reduces ammonia-producing gut bacteria; in IBS-D it may alter the microbiome and bacterial virulence and reduce low-grade inflammation.
uses: Reduction in risk of overt hepatic encephalopathy recurrence
Traveller's diarrhoea caused by non-invasive Escherichia coli

history.title: US approval
history.detail: FDA approves Xifaxan (Salix) for traveller's diarrhoea.

history.title: Hepatic encephalopathy
history.detail: FDA approves rifaximin to reduce recurrence of overt hepatic encephalopathy after a pivotal NEJM trial.

history.title: IBS-D
history.detail: FDA approves Xifaxan for irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhoea; Valeant (now Bausch Health) acquires Salix.

history.title: US generic settlement
history.detail: A patent settlement with Teva sets US generic entry for 2028.

pk.metabolism: Minimal; absorbed drug metabolised by CYP3A4

serious: Increased systemic exposure in severe hepatic impairment

facts: Rifaximin is not effective for diarrhoea caused by invasive pathogens such as Campylobacter, Shigella or Salmonella.
It is typically combined with lactulose in hepatic encephalopathy.
